audit.why: Quinn 51.62% over 587 games; early ranged dominance, losing late duel. Existing difficulty 4/10 and the Quinn-favoured early chart match the data.
audit.corrected: Kept 4/10; added the real cooldowns that decide when the lane is winnable.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes described 'all three Q casts plus W chain-pull' with no numbers.
audit.why: The Darkin Blade is 14/12/10/8/6 and Infernal Chains 20/18/16/14/12 — the 20s W at rank 1 is the whole level-3 spike window.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text and whys[2] now name the abilities and the 20s W.

audit.whatIsWrong: Text repeatedly claimed Quinn's blind makes his 'sweetspot auto' whiff, i.e. that the blind answers The Darkin Blade.
audit.why: Quinn's Q hinders vision — it denies basic attacks only. The Darkin Blade is an ability and lands through a blind; what the blind does deny is his Deathbringer Stance heal-auto. Correcting this changes how the player actually plays the trade.
audit.corrected: whys[1], wants.you[1], early and mid now separate the blinded heal-auto from the sweetspot you must sidestep.

audit.why: Vault 12/11/10/9/8, The Darkin Blade 14 to 6, Umbral Dash 9 at rank 1 — concrete windows.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[6].side said Quinn while win[6] said Skill — the two layers rendered different answers for the 2+ item row, and both the late text and the mirror say the late game splits.
audit.why: Layer disagreement; content layer is the correct one.

edits.before: Even window — his Q is online but your blind whiffs the sweetspot auto, so trades come down to who lands first.
edits.after: Even window — your blind stops his Deathbringer Stance auto, not The Darkin Blade itself, so who lands first decides it.

edits.before: He spikes here: all three Q knockups plus W chain-pull let him pull you into a full drain combo if you mistime Vault.
edits.after: He spikes here: The Darkin Blade's third swing knocks up and Infernal Chains drags you back into it if you mistime Vault.

edits.before: Aatrox spikes the moment all three Q casts plus W chain-pull are online — his sweetspot knockups turn a missed Vault into a full drain combo.
edits.after: Aatrox spikes once The Darkin Blade and Infernal Chains are online — a 20s W drag into the third-swing knockup turns a missed Vault into a full drain.

edits.before: Use Q to blind the moment he winds up a sweetspot Q so the knockup auto whiffs
edits.after: Blind as Deathbringer Stance lights up — that heal-auto whiffs, the sweetspot won't

edits.before: Land all three sweetspot Q knockups plus W chain-pull to lock you for a full drain
edits.after: Chain Infernal Chains into all three The Darkin Blade sweetspots for a full drain

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are mine — Aatrox is genuinely weak before his Q rotation comes up, so I walk him down with Harrier auto-resets and chunk him while he can only last-hit. The trick is my Q blind: the instant he winds up a sweetspot Q for the knockup, I blind him and the auto-attack portion whiffs. I never sit in W chain-pull range, because if he pulls me into a sweetspot Q he gets a free drain. Poke, reset Harrier with Vault, and back out before he can stack his combo.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are mine — Aatrox is genuinely weak before The Darkin Blade is up, so I walk him down with Harrier auto-resets and chunk him while he can only last-hit. My blind matters, but only on autos: it whiffs his Deathbringer Stance heal-auto and never the sweetspot, which I have to sidestep instead. I stay out of Infernal Chains range, a 20s cooldown at rank 1, because a drag into a sweetspot is a free drain. Poke, reset Harrier with Vault, and back out before he stacks his combo.

edits.before: By level 3 he has all his Q casts and W online and this evens out fast — his sweetspot knockups punish any greedy step-in and his passive heal eats my poke if I overstay. I keep trades short: Vault in for the Harrier proc, blind his next sweetspot, and disengage with W move speed before the third Q lands. At 6 my R is roam, not a duel button, so I shove the wave and look for a pick mid or bot rather than feeding his R combat stats by standing in lane.
edits.after: By level 3 he has all three The Darkin Blade swings and Infernal Chains and this evens out fast — the sweetspot punishes any greedy step-in and Deathbringer Stance eats my poke if I overstay. I keep trades short: Vault in for the Harrier proc, blind the heal-auto that follows, and leave on W move speed before the third swing lands. At 6 my R is roam, not a duel button, so I shove and look for a pick mid or bot rather than feeding World Ender stats in lane.

edits.before: - Aatrox The Darkin Blade: matchup-defining — Sweetspots knock up. Sidestep them. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - The Darkin Blade: 14s at rank 1, 6s at rank 5 — sidestep the sweetspots and step up while it is empty. - Umbral Dash: 9s at rank 1. - Vault: 12s, spacing only, never chip. - Behind Enemy Lines: kill windows only.

edits.before: Aatrox wastes The Darkin Blade — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: The Darkin Blade is down 14s at rank 1 — once he burns all three swings, go.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Vault is 12s at rank 1 — spend it on chip and his W lands free.

notes: The _missing feed claims World Ender can cancel Behind Enemy Lines; Riot's description gives World Ender no champion CC (it fears minions only), so no interrupt claim was written — the derived hardCC flag looks like a tooltip misfire. Same for the grounding flag on Infernal Chains: the description is drag + slow, so no grounding claim was made, matching the mirror audit's note.
